claims.statement: The proposed paid unit is a monitored connector-month or accepted incident packet, with failed sessions and unavailable time as measurable losses; no customer price or SLA-loss data is yet evidenced.
Operators, site owners, fleets, lenders, insurers, municipalities, and O&M providers are plausible reliability-budget holders, but no procurement commitment has been established.
The founder could purchase independent probes, but meaningful control also requires signed site and interface access; neither the hardware nor those permissions are currently evidenced.

AFIR and its implementing data rules establish a policy context for interoperable and real-time charging-infrastructure information, but public data alone does not prove physical session success or demand for independent meters.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Asset operations, fleet, credit-risk, insurance engineering, concession, or maintenance lead
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Stay independent of the operator, preserve signed raw evidence, test the physical session rather than only backend status, and serve multi-vendor portfolios
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Charging operator, installer, O&M provider, lender, or municipality before a direct monitoring contract
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Installer, O&M, lender, insurer, and municipal infrastructure channels

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Channel commission and technical proof-of-concept; target recovery within 25-50 monitored connectors
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Monthly or annual subscription collected in advance; hardware and installation cash precede revenue
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Unvalidated target 50-70% at dense installed sites and 25-45% for travel-heavy portable audits
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Automated active checks and alerting with field visits only for installation, calibration, or disputed evidence
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Electrical safety, payment security, cyber controls, equipment certification, professional liability, contracts, and data protection
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Hypothesis: 20-60 PLN per connector per month, 500-2000 PLN per portable audit, and separately priced incident forensics
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Probe amortization, test energy and payment transactions, connectivity, site visits, certificate signing, cloud, support, and replacement

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Charging-network software, charger OEMs, roaming platforms, and O&M firms can publish uptime and add active tests
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Paid event is a monitored connector-month or accepted incident evidence packet; measurable loss is unavailable connector time, failed sessions, SLA credits, stranded fleet time, or foregone charging revenue
commercial_mechanics.payer: Charging-site owner, fleet operator, lender, insurer, municipality, or O&M contractor
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: A portfolio enters financing, concession renewal, maintenance tender, insurance review, or repeated reliability dispute
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Annual monitoring contract renewal based on evidence coverage, detected incidents, and reduced dispute time

contrary_evidence: AFIR data standards and existing operator platforms may make independent monitoring redundant for many customers.
A true end-to-end test can require payment credentials, vehicle emulation, site access, and electrical certification that make low-cost probes impractical.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Planned purchase of replaceable test hardware paired with site-access and API credential agreements
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Use a different compliant probe supplier, perform scheduled portable tests instead of installed monitoring, or limit the report to public real-time data with a stated evidence gap
critical_control_point.current_owner: No probe fleet is evidenced; components and test equipment are currently controlled by suppliers
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Charging operator, installer, O&M provider, lender, or municipality before a direct monitoring contract
critical_control_point.duration: Hardware ownership would persist after purchase; site and interface access follow separate customer terms
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The founder has analytics capability but no evidenced charger hardware, site permission, payment credential, operator API, or monitoring customer.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: The founder can purchase or commission hardware, while each site owner controls physical access and each interface provider controls credentials
critical_control_point.renewal: Hardware is replaced or recalibrated as needed; monitoring contracts renew annually
critical_control_point.subject: Independent charger-session test probe, secure identity, and evidence-signing hardware

economics.founder_net_worth_path: Independent evidence across multi-vendor portfolios could support national recurring revenue or strategic acquisition; 5m PLN likely requires tens of thousands of monitored connectors over 5-8 years
economics.founder_time: Up to five hours per day with automated tests and qualified contractors for electrical field work
economics.gross_margin_basis: Revenue less probe amortization, installation, connectivity, test energy and payments, site work, support, security, and channel share
economics.payback: Target probe and installation payback within 12-18 months at 25-50 monitored connectors per channel deployment
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 20-60 PLN per connector per month, 500-2000 PLN per audit, plus incident forensics
economics.retention_or_repeat: Recurring connector monitoring and annual SLA evidence renewals

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Cross-operator failure signatures, recovery times, firmware patterns, and field conditions improve diagnosis and contract benchmarking
fingerprint.customer: Charging-site owners, lenders, insurers, fleet operators, municipalities, and operations contractors
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Bundle through charger installers, O&M providers, asset financiers, insurers, and municipal concession advisers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Portable or installed test hardware plus independent active checks, signed logs, alerts, and SLA-ready reports
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Asset owner, lender, insurer, or maintenance principal pays per monitored connector-month and for a verified incident report
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A charger portfolio has a financing, concession, insurance, maintenance, or revenue-share SLA that requires independent availability evidence

founder_fit: Data-science skills fit anomaly detection, availability measurement, and root-cause clustering
The product is measurable and automation-heavy after physical installation
A small multi-vendor probe fleet can be piloted below 100k PLN
Field installation and electrical safety work can be delegated to qualified contractors
risks: Unsafe or malformed tests could damage equipment or interrupt real drivers
Payment credentials and charger interfaces create cyber and fraud exposure
Travel and hardware maintenance can overwhelm subscription margin
OEMs or operators can block tests or bundle their own signed telemetry

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: per connector month independent active testing and incident evidence
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: portable or installed physical probes with independent evidence signing
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: charger payment roaming and operator interfaces needed to exercise a real session

structure.control_point: owned test probes and evidence signing at the physical connector
structure.critical_dependency: interoperable charger, payment, and operational interfaces plus lawful site access

thesis: Future operating state (2030): public and fleet chargers are financed, insured, and maintained against connector-level availability and successful-session service levels. Missing physical and contractual mechanism: an independent edge probe and signed evidence stream that tests discovery, authentication or payment, session start, energy flow, and fault recovery without relying only on the operator's own dashboard.
